claims.claim: An Ipsos poll for Global News, conducted online September 18 to 22 with 1,500 Canadian adults including 600 Alberta residents, found seven in ten Albertans plan to vote on October 19 for Alberta to remain in Canada.
claims.episode_span: Seven in ten Albertans said they plan to vote for Alberta to remain a province of Canada
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: Seven in 10 Albertans said they plan to vote for Alberta to remain a province of Canada in the upcoming referendum on Oct. 19

claims.claim: The stay figure is down two points from Ipsos polling between May 28 and June 1, a change described as statistically insignificant.
claims.episode_span: down two points from Ipsos polling between May 28 and June 1, a change Ipsos calls statistically insignificant
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: a statistically insignificant drop of two per cent from similar polling conducted between May 28 to June 1

claims.claim: Twenty percent would vote to commence a binding independence referendum, highest among men at 25 percent, Gen Z born 1997 to 2012 at 28 percent, and Albertans outside Calgary and Edmonton at 28 percent.
claims.episode_span: Twenty percent said they would vote for Alberta to commence a binding independence referendum
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: Among the 20 per cent who said they would vote for Alberta to commence the process of holding a binding independence referendum, support was highest among men (25 per cent), the Gen Z demographic born between 1997 and 2012 (28 per cent) and Albertans outside of Calgary and Edmonton (28 per cent).

claims.claim: Gregory Jack said stay-or-go numbers have not really changed and that the leave side is more motivated to turn out.
claims.episode_span: the stay-or-go numbers have not really changed through the campaign, and that turnout matters because the side that wants to leave is more motivated
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: The numbers on who wants to go or who wants to stay haven’t really changed throughout the campaign.

claims.claim: Seventy-six percent of Albertans know there are several referendum questions, and 62 percent plan to vote on all 10.
claims.episode_span: 76 percent of Albertans know the ballot has several questions, and 62 percent plan to vote on all 10
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: Ipsos found a strong majority (76 per cent) of Albertans are aware there are several questions in the upcoming referendum, and 62 per cent plan to vote on all 10 referendum questions.

claims.claim: Premier Danielle Smith added a tenth separatism question on May 21 to a referendum announced February 19 that began with nine questions on immigration and the Constitution.
claims.episode_span: Premier Danielle Smith added the separatism question on May 21 to a referendum announced February 19
claims.source_title: As referendum looms, 70% of Albertans want province to remain in Canada
claims.supporting_quote: The referendum, announced Feb. 19, initially contained nine questions pertaining to immigration and the Constitution.

claims.claim: John Thune said the Senate returns next week and is teeing up a test vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act so large data centers pay for grid upgrades.
claims.episode_span: a test vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act front and center
claims.source_title: Senate plots its final week before elections with potential data center electricity vote
claims.supporting_quote: He specifically noted a test vote on legislation known as the Ratepayer Protection Act, which is intended to address rising electricity prices by requiring state regulators to consider adopting standards to ensure that large data centers pay for needed electric grid upgrades.

claims.claim: The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3, and Democrats blocked Jon Husted from clearing it for President Trump’s signature.
claims.episode_span: The House passed it last week, 417 to 3, and Democrats blocked Senator Jon Husted
claims.source_title: Senate plots its final week before elections with potential data center electricity vote
claims.supporting_quote: The House passed the bill last week by a vote of 417-3, but Democrats blocked an effort by Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, to clear the measure for President Donald Trump’s signature.

claims.claim: Inside Elections rates Husted’s race against Sherrod Brown a toss-up, and Schumer called Husted’s bill a voluntary fraud compared with a mandatory Democratic bill.
claims.episode_span: Schumer, Democrat of New York, said Wednesday that Husted’s bill is voluntary and “a fraud”
claims.source_title: Senate plots its final week before elections with potential data center electricity vote
claims.supporting_quote: “Sen. Husted’s bill is a fraud. It’s voluntary, no company has to do it. The bill we have is mandatory. It is much stronger and is what is needed,” Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., said Wednesday.

claims.claim: Melania Trump described an AI educator named Plato, and Alpha School is the administration showcase for two hours a day of AI instruction.
claims.episode_span: imagine an AI humanoid educator named Plato giving children classical studies at home
claims.source_title: Why so many Republicans are rejecting Trump’s AI vision for education
claims.supporting_quote: “Imagine a humanoid educator named ‘Plato,’” she said.

claims.claim: Alpha says students learn 2.6 times faster, a claim no outside researcher has verified, and Florida, Iowa, and Utah have limited AI and screens in schools.
claims.episode_span: Alpha says students learn 2.6 times faster; Vox reports no outside researcher has verified that.
claims.source_title: Why so many Republicans are rejecting Trump’s AI vision for education
claims.supporting_quote: Alpha says its students learn 2.6 times faster with two hours a day of AI instruction. No outside researcher has verified that, though studies may soon launch.

claims.claim: USDA is reopening the Santa Teresa, New Mexico, cattle port despite a fresh screwworm case.
claims.episode_span: reopening the Santa Teresa, New Mexico, port of entry to live cattle from Mexico despite a fresh screwworm case
claims.source_title: USDA to Reopen Major New Mexico Cattle Port Despite Fresh Screwworm Case
claims.supporting_quote: USDA to Reopen Major New Mexico Cattle Port Despite Fresh Screwworm Case

claims.claim: Pentagon officials are pushing a record $1.5 trillion budget request, and some GOP senators say the effort came too late.
claims.episode_span: President Trump’s record $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget request, while some Republican senators worry the closed-door push came too late
claims.source_title: Pentagon turns on the jets in $1.5 trillion defense budget push
claims.supporting_quote: Pentagon officials have ramped up their efforts in recent weeks to help Congress carve a path toward President Trump’s record $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget request.

claims.claim: Recalled internal charts obtained by The Hill and NewsNation show civil-division attorneys have plummeted under the Trump administration as caseloads surge.
claims.episode_span: the number of attorneys in the Justice Department’s civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration as civil caseloads surge
claims.source_title: Internal DOJ charts show agency bleeding staff as caseloads surge
claims.supporting_quote: A series of charts, apparently inadvertently shared and then recalled, show how the number of attorneys within the civil division has plummeted under the Trump administration.

claims.claim: Republican senators are dismayed by Trump’s welcome of Xi after Iran used Chinese satellite imagery to target US troops in Jordan.
claims.episode_span: Iran used Chinese satellite imagery to target US troops in Jordan
claims.source_title: GOP senators dismayed by Trump embrace of Xi after China helped Iran target US troops
claims.supporting_quote: Republican senators are expressing concern and dismay over President Trump’s lavish welcome of Chinese President Xi Jinping to a two-day summit in Washington after it was revealed earlier this month that Iran used Chinese satellite imagery to target U.S. troops in Jordan.

claims.claim: Bill C-2 returns to second reading after the government removed warrantless-access provisions; it was first called on September 17, 2025, and the motion would send it to the public safety committee.
claims.episode_span: The government has removed provisions that would have allowed law enforcement warrantless access
claims.source_title: Parliament Today: Strong Borders Act returns to second reading
claims.supporting_quote: The government has since removed provisions that would have given law enforcement warrantless access powers, narrowing the bill from the version originally tabled.

claims.claim: Anandasangaree cited Bills C-14, C-16, and C-9 as safety legislation, and Fraser said the government would act on expert and police advice.
claims.episode_span: citing Bill C-14 on bail and sentencing, Bill C-16 on victims’ rights, and Bill C-9 on community safety
claims.source_title: Parliament Today: Strong Borders Act returns to second reading
claims.supporting_quote: Bill C-14 strengthens bail as well as sentencing. Bill C-16 ensures that victims’ rights are protected. Bill C-9 ensures the safety and security of communities.
